All 36 state Houses of Assembly have approved the proposed constitutional amendment to establish state police, now awaiting transmission to President Bola Tinubu for assent. The Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, disclosed this in a statement on Monday, describing the unanimous endorsement as an unprecedented demonstration of cooperation between the federal and state legislatures. The development means the bill has secured 100 per cent approval from the state assemblies, exceeding the constitutional requirement of at least 24 states under Section 9(2) of the 1999 Constitution. Ogunlana said the bill had satisfied all constitutional and administrative requirements for transmission but that the National Assembly leadership delayed the process briefly to allow for broader national consensus and engagement with all states. He said, “Following the completion of the verification process by my office, the Bill is set for transmission to the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, for His Excellency’s assent.” Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources The bill, known as the Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill to provide for the establishment of State Police Services and related matters, is designed to amend the 1999 Constitution to provide a legal framework for the establishment of state-controlled police formations. Ogunlana said the unanimous approval reflected cooperation between the National Assembly and state legislatures, as well as constructive engagement between the executive arms of government at both federal and state levels. He commended the 36 state governors, speakers and members of the state House of Assembly as well as other stakeholders, for their contributions to the process. Aka urges Tinubu to reward African Scrabble champions FG targets telecom access for all Delta communities by 2027 Evening recap: Tinubu frees 78 suspects, only 14 states pay pensions, other stories The clerk added that the development would provide a foundation for the National Assembly to transmit other Sixth Constitution Alteration Bills to the state Houses of Assembly for consideration. The approval came barely 24 hours after the Senate Leader, Opeyemi Bamidele, disclosed that 32 state assemblies had endorsed the proposed state police legislation, with reports from the remaining four still being awaited. Bamidele had said the four outstanding assemblies were expected to submit their reports by Tuesday ahead of the National Assembly’s resumption. He had also indicated that the National Assembly was preparing to proceed with the next stage of the constitutional amendment process once the outstanding reports were received. With all 36 assemblies now having approved the bill, attention has shifted to its formal transmission to Tinubu for his assent, which would pave the way for the implementation of the constitutional framework for state police. The PUNCH reports that the bill may be presented to President Bola Tinubu on Friday.
